name: In f(R), scalar-tensor, Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet and higher-curvature theories the field equations rearrange to G = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective

source.located: Primary: Sotiriou & Faraoni, 'f(R) theories of gravity', Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 451 (2010), arXiv:0805.1726v4 -- eq (6) metric f(R) field eqs, eqs (10)-(12) the effective-stress rearrangement, p.6 text on it, eq (28) Palatini form, eq (55) Brans-Dicke omega=0 form, p.17 energy-condition caveat. Supporting, read at source: Lobo & Oliveira arXiv:0909.5539 (Phys. Rev. D 80, 104012, 2009) eqs (2)-(21), the published 'matter satisfies the energy conditions, T_eff violates NEC' construction; Bronnikov, Skvortsova & Starobinsky arXiv:1005.3262 (2010) -- the no-wormhole theorem in scalar-tensor and F(R) gravity (restating Bronnikov-Starobinsky gr-qc/0612032, JETP Lett. 85, 1 (2007), which is NAMED-NOT-READ here); Glavan & Lin arXiv:1905.03601 p.1 (Gauss-Bonnet contribution vanishes identically in D=4) and Guerses, Sisman & Tekin arXiv:2004.03390 p.1-4 (same, and the 4D limit contested); Capozziello, Lobo & Mimoso arXiv:1407.7293 eqs (26)-(33). The tree cites no source for this result; the audit takes the canonical review statement.

published_statement: Sotiriou-Faraoni 0805.1726 p.6: 'it is possible to write the field equations in the form of Einstein equations with an effective stress-energy tensor composed of curvature terms moved to the right hand side. This approach is questionable in principle (the theory is not Einstein's theory and it is artificial to force upon it an interpretation in terms of Einstein equations) but, in practice, it has been proved to be useful in scalar-tensor gravity.' Eq (10): G_mn = kappa T_mn / f'(R) + g_mn [f(R) - R f'(R)] / (2 f'(R)) + [nabla_m nabla_n f'(R) - g_mn box f'(R)] / f'(R); eq (11): G_mn = (kappa/f'(R)) (T_mn + T^(eff)_mn), 'G_eff = G/f'(R) can be regarded as the effective gravitational coupling ... positivity of G_eff (equivalent to the requirement that the graviton is not a ghost) imposes that f'(R) > 0'; eq (12) T^(eff); 'The effective energy density derived from it is not positive-definite and none of the energy conditions holds. Again, this situation is analogous to that occurring in scalar-tensor gravity.' p.17: imposing energy conditions on T^(eff) 'is not very meaningful from the physical point of view since ... effective stress-energy terms originating from the geometry ... do, in general, violate all the energy conditions'. Scalar-tensor (BD omega=0) form eq (55): G_mn = (kappa/phi) T_mn - g_mn V(phi)/(2 phi) + (1/phi)(nabla_m nabla_n phi - g_mn box phi). Palatini eq (28): 'the modified source on the right hand side ... includes derivatives of the stress-energy tensor'. Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet: 'In D = 4 the Gauss-Bonnet invariant is a total derivative, and hence does not contribute to the gravitational dynamics ... vanishing identically in D = 4, but not in D >= 5' (Glavan-Lin 1905.03601 p.1); 'for D = 4, the H_mn tensor vanishes identically and hence ... the field equations reduce to the Einstein's theory' (Guerses-Sisman-Tekin 2004.03390 p.1). Negativity with normal matter: Lobo-Oliveira 0909.5539 abstract 'We impose that the matter threading the wormhole satisfies the energy conditions, so that it is the effective stress-energy tensor containing higher order curvature derivatives that is responsible for the null energy condition violation'. Counter-statement: Bronnikov-Skvortsova-Starobinsky 1005.3262 abstract 'in cases where a wormhole is obtained, the effective gravitational constant G_eff is negative in some region of space, i.e., the graviton becomes a ghost ... special wormhole solutions are only possible if F(R) contains an extremum at which G_eff changes its sign'; p.6 on Lobo-Oliveira's examples: 'in the first two examples, Eqs. (25), (31) of that paper, F_R is negative over some range of R for matter satisfying the weak energy condition'.
published_hypotheses: METRIC f(R) (SF eq 5-6): action (1/2kappa) int sqrt(-g) f(R) + S_M(g, psi); matter MINIMALLY coupled to g, hence nabla^m T_mn = 0 (SF p.5 'In metric f(R) gravity the matter is minimally coupled to the metric ... T_mn is divergence-free'). Without minimal coupling (f(R,T), f(R,L_m)) nabla T != 0 (Capozziello-Lobo-Mimoso 1407.7293 eq 32-33).
the rearranged matter coupling is kappa/f'(R), not kappa: G = (kappa/f')(T + T_eff) (SF eq 11); T_eff in SF eq (12) is built from f, R and derivatives of f'(R) ONLY in this 1/f' normalisation

f'(R) > 0 for a non-ghost graviton / positive G_eff (SF p.6, p.16 'we assume that f' > 0 ... and f'' > 0 to avoid the Dolgov-Kawasaki instability'); f'' != 0 for the scalar-tensor equivalence (SF p.12)

SCALAR-TENSOR (SF eq 55; Bronnikov et al. eq 1): T_eff is built from the scalar phi (its derivatives and potential V(phi)), with coupling kappa/phi; non-ghost requires f(Phi) > 0 and l(Phi) = f h + (3/2)(df/dPhi)^2 > 0 (1005.3262 eq 2)
PALATINI f(R) (SF eq 28): the effective source contains the matter trace and its derivatives (f' = f'(R(T)))

EINSTEIN-GAUSS-BONNET: the Gauss-Bonnet tensor H_mn is non-zero only for D >= 5; in D = 4 it vanishes identically (Glavan-Lin p.1; Guerses et al. p.1); a 4D effect needs either a scalar coupled to GB (EsGB, 2609.18475 p.1 'a dynamical scalar coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant keeps the higher-curvature term active') or the D->4 limit of alpha/(D-4), which Guerses-Sisman-Tekin argue 'does not exist in four dimensions'

the rearrangement is an interpretation, not a physical source: SF p.6 'questionable in principle', p.17 energy conditions on T_eff 'not very meaningful'; Capozziello-Lobo-Mimoso p.5 'somewhat misleading to call these impositions as energy conditions'

NEGATIVITY UNDER NORMAL MATTER, as published (Lobo-Oliveira): static spherically symmetric, CONSTANT redshift function Phi' = 0, anisotropic fluid, specific shape functions; the examples (25), (31) have F = f'(R) < 0 (Bronnikov et al. p.6; computed here)

NO-GO (Bronnikov-Starobinsky gr-qc/0612032 as restated in 1005.3262 p.1-2, p.5-6): static, asymptotically flat (twice) wormholes are absent in scalar-tensor theory with f(Phi) > 0 and l(Phi) > 0 everywhere, and in F(R) with F_R > 0 everywhere, if matter respects the NEC; exceptions need F_R -> 0 (conformal continuation, G_eff < 0 beyond)
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED -- the coupling. overturn.py:237 writes G_munu = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective with coefficient 8 pi; SF eq (10)-(11) (0805.1726 p.6) has kappa T/f'(R). The tree's form is reachable only by moving kappa (1/f' - 1) T into T^effective, and then T^effective CONTAINS THE MATTER TENSOR (computed, check A2: T_eff(tree) = kappa T (1/F - 1) + kappa T_eff^SF/F, exact). So overturn.py:239 'T^effective is built from curvature' is false in the tree's own normalisation unless f' == 1 (GR). Discrepancy of presentation, not of existence: the rearrangement itself is an identity (check A).

DROPPED -- scalar-tensor content. overturn.py:234-239 says T^effective is 'built from curvature' for scalar-tensor theories; SF eq (55) and 1407.7293 eq (47) build it from the scalar phi, its derivatives and V(phi) (and for Palatini f(R), SF eq 28, from the matter trace and its derivatives). Check A3 confirms SF eq (55) = eq (10) under phi = F, V = R F - f.

DROPPED -- the dimension hypothesis for Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet. overturn.py:234-235 lists 'Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet' without D >= 5. In D = 4 H_mn == 0 identically (Glavan-Lin 1905.03601 p.1; Guerses-Sisman-Tekin 2004.03390 p.1), machine-checked here on generic exact curvature jets (check B: H_mn == 0 exactly in D=4 on three random jets with GB scalar != 0; H != 0 in D=5; trace H = -(D-4)/2 GB exactly). So 4D EGB supplies T^effective == 0; a 4D effect needs EsGB (a scalar coupled to GB) or the Glavan-Lin alpha/(D-4) limit, which is contested (2004.03390: 'does not admit an intrinsically four-dimensional definition').

DROPPED -- minimal matter coupling. overturn.py:235 'any higher-curvature theory': the conservation nabla T^matter = 0 (so nabla T^effective = 0 by Bianchi) needs matter minimally coupled (SF p.5); for curvature-matter couplings the matter tensor is not conserved (1407.7293 eq 32-33). The rearrangement as a bare identity (T_eff := G - 8 pi T) survives any metric theory, which is also why it carries no physical content by itself (SF p.6 'questionable in principle').

DROPPED -- the no-ghost condition. overturn.py:239-241 'An effective term can be negative where the matter term is not. If it can, L2 breaks'; SF p.6 and p.16 make f'(R) > 0 the non-ghost condition, and Bronnikov-Skvortsova-Starobinsky 1005.3262 show that wormhole solutions with NEC-respecting matter in scalar-tensor / F(R) gravity require G_eff < 0 somewhere. Computed here: both published WEC-respecting f(R) wormhole examples (Lobo-Oliveira eq 25 and eq 31) have F = f'(R) < 0 throughout (check C iii; ex.(31) is exactly f = -R, GR with G -> -G), and in the static Phi' = 0 class on Lobo's eq (16) rho = F rho_eff exactly, so rho >= 0 with rho_eff < 0 forces F < 0 (check D). EVIDENCE THE OTHER WAY (check E): f = R - 2 Lambda, Lambda < 0, F = 1 > 0 gives effective energy density Lambda < 0 under any matter, no ghost -- so the bare existence claim 'can be negative' stands without a ghost; the no-ghost narrowing bites on the wormhole/throat use (Bronnikov-Starobinsky), not on the sentence as a sentence.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0, ~15 s. (A) SF eq (6) <=> eq (10)/(11)/(12) holds identically on a general static spherical metric (Phi(r), b(r)) with arbitrary F(r), f(r) -- the rearrangement is an identity. (A2) in the tree's 8 pi normalisation T_eff = kappa T (1/F - 1) + kappa T_eff^SF/F exactly: matter sits inside T_eff unless F == 1. (A3) SF eq (55) == eq (10) under phi = F, V = RF - f. (B) exact rational curvature jets: Gauss-Bonnet tensor H_mn == 0 exactly in D = 4 on three random jets (GB scalar 579.5, -361.8, -2595, all != 0), H != 0 in D = 5 (max |H| = 5466), trace H = -(D-4)/2 GB exactly in both. (C) Lobo-Oliveira: R = 2b'/r^2 and box F match their eqs (14)-(15); eqs (16)-(18) satisfy (10)-(12), and on them H = (FR + box F + T)/4 == 0 identically; (10)-(12) are invariant under rho -> rho - l, p_r,p_t -> p + l for arbitrary l(r), so (16)-(18) are one member of a family fixed only by the trace equation (3) with f_R = F. (C iii) ex.(31) (C1 = -1, alpha = -1): F == -1, matter rho = r0^2/r^4 > 0, rho + p_r >= 0, rho_eff + p_r^eff = -2 r0^2/r^4 < 0, and f from eq (3) is exactly -R (consistent; GR with the sign of G flipped). ex.(25) (C1 = 0, C2 = -1): F <= -1 < 0, T = 0 confirmed. (D) static Phi' = 0 metric f(R): rho = f/2 - box F exactly; eq (16) is the true density iff f = FR + 2 box F; on eq (16) rho = F rho_eff. (E) f = R - 2 Lambda: T_eff(tree) = -Lambda delta, effective density Lambda (negative for Lambda < 0, F = 1). TWO SOURCE DISCREPANCIES recorded, not refutations: (1) Lobo-Oliveira eq (34) as extracted, at alpha = -1, gives df/dR = -5 at R/R0 = 1/4 where eq (31)/(3) require f = -R (df/dR = -1) -- PDF extraction or misprint, unresolved here; (2) for ex.(25), f(R) reconstructed from trace eq (3) (their eq 29, f = -R F) fails df/dR = F (residual df/dr - F dR/dr = 12.56, 0.685, 0.0757 at r/r0 = 1.25, 2, 3), so the published rho(16) is not the matter density of a metric-f(R) solution; enforcing f = int F dR shifts rho (e.g. 0.815 -> 2.278 at r = 1.25 r0 with integration constant 0) while rho + p_r is invariant, so the NEC-type sign they report survives and WEC can be met by choice of the constant. Neither discrepancy moves the tree's claim.

later_literature.what: Static, (twice) asymptotically flat wormholes cannot be supported by NEC-respecting matter in scalar-tensor theory with f(Phi) > 0 and l(Phi) > 0, nor in F(R) with F_R > 0 everywhere; claimed f(R) wormholes (Lobo-Oliveira 0909.5539) have F_R < 0 over some range or F_R -> 0 at the throat. The effective term can be negative, but a throat built from it with normal matter needs a ghost graviton somewhere.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: 'previous physicists may have all lacked certain data'. For THIS result the evidence is against it mattering. The rearrangement is an algebraic identity (check A, exact on a general static spherical metric with arbitrary F, f) and the existence of a negative effective term is an identity-level fact (check E: f = R - 2 Lambda, Lambda < 0, F = 1); no measured quantity enters either, so no datum the authors lacked (Sotiriou-Faraoni 2008-2010; Lobo-Oliveira 2009; Bronnikov et al. 2007-2010) could change them. What later work supplied was not data but THEOREMS AND CRITIQUES that narrow the use: the Bronnikov-Starobinsky no-ghost wormhole theorem (2007/2010), the 4D Gauss-Bonnet vanishing and the contested Glavan-Lin limit (2019-2020), and the minimal-coupling caveat (2015). Observational bounds that post-date the review (e.g. the 2017 binary-neutron-star GW speed measurement Glavan-Lin mention at p.3; solar-system f(R) bounds SF discuss in sec V) constrain how LARGE T_eff may be in the regimes they probe; they were not read here at the numerical level and cannot move an identity. So: the inputs missing in the original literature do not change the conclusion; the incompleteness M suspects is real but lies in the TREE'S restatement (8 pi coupling, 'built from curvature', EGB without D >= 5, the no-ghost condition), not in the published result.
grade_evidence: The published result STANDS as published: the metric f(R) rearrangement G = (kappa/f')(T + T_eff) is an exact identity (check A; SF 0805.1726 eq 6 -> 10-12), its scalar-tensor form is SF eq (55) (check A3), and an effective term can be negative (SF p.6 'not positive-definite'; check E with F = 1; Lobo-Oliveira construction re-derived, check C). The TREE'S use (overturn.py:234-241) holds on a smaller class than stated: (i) with coefficient 8 pi, T^effective contains kappa (1/f' - 1) T^matter (check A2), so 'built from curvature' holds only in the kappa/f' normalisation; for scalar-tensor it is built from phi, for Palatini from the matter trace (SF eq 28, 55); (ii) Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet contributes T^effective == 0 identically in D = 4 (check B, exact; Glavan-Lin p.1; Guerses et al. p.1) -- a 4D effect needs EsGB or the contested alpha/(D-4) limit; (iii) 'any higher-curvature theory' needs minimal matter coupling for a conserved T^matter (SF p.5; 1407.7293 eq 32-33); (iv) the f' > 0 no-ghost hypothesis is dropped, and for the wormhole/throat use it is load-bearing: Bronnikov-Skvortsova-Starobinsky (1005.3262) show static AF wormholes with NEC-respecting matter need G_eff < 0 somewhere, both published WEC-respecting f(R) examples have F < 0 (check C iii), and in the static Phi' = 0 class on Lobo's eq (16) rho = F rho_eff (check D). Not WRONG: nothing refutes the sentence 'an effective term can be negative where the matter term is not' (check E gives a ghost-free instance, though it is GR + Lambda). Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters. Two discrepancies in Lobo-Oliveira (eq 34 as extracted; ex.(25) f_R != F) are recorded as discrepancies, not refutations, and do not move the grade.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the result with coupling kappa/f' (or declares T^effective to include the matter-coupling shift), names D >= 5 or a scalar-GB coupling for EGB, names minimal coupling, and names f' > 0 / G_eff > 0 as a hypothesis the L2 break must meet or explicitly waive. To WRONG: only a demonstrated error in the rearrangement identity itself (check A refutes that on the static spherical class; a general-metric symbolic check would close it everywhere). To OPEN on the EGB clause: if the tree means the Glavan-Lin 4D theory, its status is contested (1905.03601 vs 2004.03390) and that sub-clause would be OPEN rather than NARROWED. The no-ghost narrowing would lift if a ghost-free (F_R > 0, l > 0) static configuration with NEC-respecting matter and negative Misner-Sharp mass from T_eff were exhibited -- check E (Lambda < 0) is ghost-free but is GR + Lambda, not a higher-curvature effect.
